slides.title: No One Wins in Nuclear War: A Social Simulation of Military Decision-making
slides.highlight: WOPR provides a verifiable rules engine for social simulations of organizational decision-making, supporting collective command-and-control systems and private-channel negotiation. This is relevant to MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent models.

card.one_liner: WOPR is a social-simulation environment for studying high-stakes organizational decision-making via a verifiable rules engine.
card.key_idea: A deterministic, replay-validated engine using a decision-point contract, a four-rung communication 'press ladder', and four command-and-control archetypes for collective faction decision-making.
card.evaluation: Verified via a 240-game sweep confirming seeded outcomes are preserved; instantiated using the card game Nuclear War with a rule conformance matrix.
card.limitation: Early-stage tool; lacks controlled studies, large-scale press mode evaluation, and automatic enforcement of agent commitments.

slides.title: Cocktail-Talker: Multi-Speaker Dialog Modeling in Noisy Social Environments with Turn Action GRPO
slides.tldr: MULTI-SPEAKER DIALOG MODELING IN NOISY ENVIRONMENTS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a speech LLM framework that uses action tokens to decide whether to respond, listen, or ignore in multi-speaker settings, supporting HyECHO's goals in addressee modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: Cocktail-Talker enables speech assistants to selectively respond, listen, or ignore in noisy multi-speaker environments.
card.key_idea: A Qwen2.5-Omni-based framework using three action tokens, trained via SFT and GRPO reinforcement learning on simulated multi-speaker dialogs from the Cocktail-DialogGen pipeline.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on seen/unseen environments using binary Respond/Silent accuracy and response quality metrics (METEOR, ROUGE-L). Results show significant improvement over baseline speech LLMs.
card.limitation: The system is not streaming, assumes fixed turn boundaries, and lacks visual or spatial sensors for speaker inference.

slides.title: Hybrid Attention Estimation Pipeline for Adaptive HRI Using an Expressive Robotic Head
slides.tldr: HYBRID ATTENTION ESTIMATION FOR ADAPTIVE HRI
slides.highlight: This work proposes a pipeline combining geometric and semantic perception to regulate adaptive interaction behaviors in an expressive robotic head, contributing to the development of embodied social robots for RwB.

card.one_liner: A hybrid attention pipeline for an InMoov robotic head enabling adaptive pause-and-resume interaction behaviors.
card.key_idea: Combines a fast geometric layer (MediaPipe head-pose) for real-time state regulation with a semantic layer (VLM) for contextual attention labeling via a finite state machine.
card.evaluation: Tested with 10 participants over 40 trials. Results showed reliable interaction starts and successful adaptive pausing/resuming in distraction scenarios.
card.limitation: Controlled experimental setup, small participant sample, and lack of manual frame-level ground truth for attention labels.

slides.title: DuplexGen: Adaptive Synthesis of Human-AI Turn-Taking Dialogues
slides.highlight: Introduces DuplexGen, a framework that uses human preference annotations to generate dialogues with scenario-specific turn-taking behaviors. This is relevant to HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement in hybrid human-AI team states.

slides.title: Neuro-Symbolic Participation Governance for Verifiable AI Agents in Open Digital Twin Ecosystems
slides.tldr: NEURO-SYMBOLIC GOVERNANCE FOR VERIFIABLE AI AGENTS
slides.highlight: This work proposes a neuro-symbolic framework to bridge neural reasoning with deterministic governance for verifiable AI agents, supporting the MIMIC goal of simulating harmonious hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: A decentralized governance framework using neuro-symbolic profiles and blockchain to verify AI agent capabilities and compliance.
card.key_idea: Binds LLM agents to symbolic domain ontologies via Verifiable Credentials, using blockchain smart contracts for identity verification, dynamic role binding, and immutable interaction logging.
card.evaluation: Tested with 42 cases (security, policy, scalability) using a healthcare prototype; achieved 100% attack detection and O(1) verification complexity.
card.limitation: Focuses on admission governance and provenance; does not verify the actual quality or correctness of the agent's clinical recommendations.

slides.title: VAmoS Bench: Voice Agent Simulation Bench
slides.highlight: This benchmark evaluates end-to-end voice agent performance in stateful customer-support tasks, contributing to HyECHO's focus on modeling engagement and interaction within hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: VAmoS Bench evaluates end-to-end voice agents using stateful customer-support simulations with joint speech and execution grading.
card.key_idea: A simulation framework using 100 banking scenarios with isolated PostgreSQL backends, grading agents on a combined record of transcripts and tool-invocation traces to detect say/do mismatches.
card.evaluation: Eleven voice agent stacks were tested across 3,300 phone calls. Metrics include task completion (43.0%–71.0%), latency, cost, and barge-in rates.
card.limitation: Limited to one banking domain; relies on a single LLM judge and synthetic users without human-annotated gold sets.

slides.title: AtmosERC: Modeling Dialogue-Level Affective Atmosphere for Emotion Recognition in Conversation
slides.highlight: This work introduces AtmosERC to capture dialogue-level affective atmosphere and speaker-conditioned priors, contributing to the multimodal social perception of team states for HyECHO.

card.one_liner: AtmosERC improves conversation emotion recognition by using a dialogue-level affective atmosphere as a global prior.
card.key_idea: It extracts a stable affective atmosphere vector via relation-aware graph filtering, which serves as a reusable prior for either lightweight models or LLM-based prompting.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on IEMOCAP, MELD, EmoryNLP, and DailyDialog against sequence, transformer, and graph baselines; results show consistent improvements over global context pooling.
card.limitation: A gap exists between predicted atmosphere descriptors and gold-proxy dominant emotions, indicating room for better estimation and verbalization.
